text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.74% today after oil prices climbed on geopolitical tension — specifically, reporting that the U.S. is preparing for potential Iran strikes following midterm elections. With crude at $103/barrel domestically and $123/barrel globally, the prospect of Middle East conflict disrupting supply lifts the entire energy sector and benefits major oil producers like this company. The stock had already jumped sharply on October 23rd ($145→$151) when this energy trade narrative was gaining momentum.

The broader backdrop amplifies today's move: oil-dependent businesses are already feeling pressure from high fuel costs (as seen in the cruise industry), and any further supply disruptions would push prices higher still — benefiting integrated producers with exploration and production assets.
